facts.fact: Deliberation 005/2025 of the data protection authority (APD), adopted 30 July 2025, requires public- and private-sector controllers using cloud services abroad to obtain prior APD authorisation, with a separate foreign-transfer authorisation request where the host country is not on the country list published in deliberation 004/2025. The text is the amended version published 2026-04-30.

The amended deliberation 005/2025 refers to a list of countries published in the APD's deliberation 004/2025, with a hosting choice limited to countries offering adequate protection as that deliberation determines; dated by the 30 July 2025 adoption.

The agenda of the APD monthly meeting of 29 April 2026 lists discussion and approval of amending certain articles of deliberation 2025/004, which fixes the conditions, rules and procedures for transferring personal data abroad, and of deliberation 2025/005 on cloud outsourcing abroad; the passage shown does not give the outcome.

facts.fact: Deliberation 005/2025 of the data protection authority (APD), adopted 30 July 2025, requires public- and private-sector controllers using cloud services abroad to obtain prior APD authorisation, with a separate foreign-transfer authorisation request where the host country is not on the country list published in deliberation 004/2025.
Deliberation 005/2025 refers to a list of countries published in the APD's deliberation 004/2025 that determines which host countries offer adequate protection.

Deliberation 004/2025 of the APD, adopted 14 July 2025 under article 73 of law 2017-020, sets the conditions, rules and procedures for transferring personal data abroad, with article 21 of the law having the APD publish and update a list of countries it judges adequate.

facts.fact: Articles 20 to 25 of Loi n° 2017-020 (Journal Officiel no. 1400, dated 22 July 2017) bar a data controller from transferring personal data to a third country unless it ensures a sufficient level of protection, with exceptions for one-off non-massive transfers on express consent or on stated necessity, and with authorisation by the data protection authority (APD) on guarantees such as contract clauses; the document is the enacted text and gives no repeal.
